beats.t: The market's star lamps went out one by one. The star people folded their tents and left. Only one charcoal fire remained in Yundal's tent.
Moka wasn't grilling. He simply held a metal skewer and watched the coals. His whiskers still trembled now and then.
Moka. That voice earlier. Who was it?
A kid used to sing on the festival island. Museong. Huge voice. Terrible at keeping time.
Couldn't sing?
Terrible. But he looked happy. Always closed his eyes onstage. Said looking at the audience made him nervous.
A spark jumped from the coals. Moka pressed it out with the skewer's tip. His grip tightened.
One year, at the sunrise concert, his voice cracked. First line. Really loudly.
And?
Everyone laughed. From the next day, he was gone. A few years later, the crow came. Saying anyone who sings gets mocked.
Moka stopped. His face held something more, swallowed back. Yeoni didn't ask. It was a face that would speak someday without being asked.
You said a boy's face showed beneath the crow mask on the Island of Expression. If that boy guards a gate here, there must be a reason.
Black Moon brought him, probably. Said it would collect his feathers. Even his remaining song.
That damned eclipse. Why keep taking other people's songs?
A low breath came from beyond the coals. Neo leaned against a tent pole with his eyes closed. His right arm was black to the elbow.
Neo. It's farther up than before.
Said I'd tell you when it spread. Telling you now. It spread.
How can you say it so calmly?!
Yundal reopened the chart on the table. The Wu space was blacker than before. Black energy stretched into its neighbor like thread.
Obstruction Transformation can't be erased. It's a label attached by your birth year. As long as you were born in an Im year, Obstruction attaching to Wu Qu is fixed.
Then there's no way?
Can't erase it doesn't mean no way. Obstruction resembles a debt. A stagnant place where something owed was never received. Black Moon uses that place like a straw.
(Debt. Uncollected. Just like the words she always used.)
To pull out the straw, we first need to see what's stuck inside that room. The Wu room. We have to enter the Career Palace.
I'll go.
No. That's where it eats Metal. You're the last person who should go.
That's why I have to. Wu Qu is a Metal star. I'm the one that door can respond to.
...True. The Career Palace door only responds to Metal. And Mr. Cat is the only Metal in your chart.
Tell me things like that beforehand!
I just did. Must have caught Mr. Cat's habits.
Yeoni bit their lip. They wanted to shout at the black space, at Neo enduring with that calm face, at the eclipse calling them a vessel.
(Hold it in. Shout, and Neo gets hurt. But only holding it in makes fire rot.)
Then together. You absolutely don't go alone. That's the condition.
Negotiating now, too.
Graduate of the island that sold time.
The way to the Wu gate lay at the palace's southern edge. The sky darkened as they went. Stars had gone out one by one, as though drowned in black water.
Gray-faced star people lined up. At the line's end stood a high judgment bench. Something in a black cloak sat atop it.
Next.
The person at the front offered a lantern. The figure struck its hammer. Light drew from the lantern like thread and streamed through the door behind the bench.
Confiscated. Crime: laughing.
Taking their light for laughing?
Shh. Behind the bench is the Career Palace. All the stolen light goes there. To Wu Qu.
The crow. The same black mask and cloak from the Island of Expression. But one feather at its chest was unusually black. Like charcoal. Like ink.
(That feather. Same color as the black thing clinging to Wu Qu on the chart.)
Look. Blackness runs from that feather into the door.
Moka was right. An ink-like thread streamed from the chest feather into the doorway. It pulsed as though alive.
That's the straw. The root of Obstruction Transformation. The crow holds Black Moon's straw planted in this sky.
Yundal proposed a plan. Disguise themselves as gray faces and join the line. He removed his glove and offered his right hand to Yeoni.
I'll draw in your light briefly. Your face will turn gray. I'll return it once we're through.
But that hurts your hand.
It does. I'll put it on your tab.
A black hole sat at the palm's center. The surrounding flesh cracked like a broken vessel. Wider than when Yeoni first saw it.
The hole inhaled. Warmth drained from Yeoni's cheeks. They knew without a mirror. Their face had turned ash gray.
...Urgh. Your light is hotter than I expected.
Me too. Hurry.
Mr. Otter's expression is already gray.
You con artist!
Moka disguised himself in gray, too. But Neo's Metal could not be concealed. He would hide behind a pillar beside the line and wait for the door to open.
(Gray face. So this is what the people on the Island of Expression felt. Nothing seems like it would taste good.)
The line shortened. The bench drew near. Yeoni's turn. They offered empty hands instead of a lantern.
Your lantern.
Don't have one. Never did.
No light, nothing to confiscate. Pass.
Yeoni passed the bench. Next, Moka. He lowered his gray face. But...
His tail tapped the floor. Tap, tap. A rhythm. Unconsciously. The beat he always hummed by the charcoal.
...That rhythm just now.
No rhythm. My tail just does that.
Lies. Confiscated.
The hammer rose. At that moment, the door behind the bench rattled. A metallic sound came through the crack. It was trying to open on its own, toward the pillar's shadow.
The door reacted to Mr. Cat's Metal! Now!
Neo ran from the shadows, vaulted over the bench, and touched the door. As it opened, Yeoni, Moka, and Yundal rushed after him.
Intruders! Metal! Metal has entered!
The Career Palace resembled an iron temple. Walls and pillars, all metal. But rusted. Black rust. Ash-gray lanterns lay piled like mountains on the floor.
Two great stars floated at the center. One shone heavily in earthy light. The other gleamed like metal, its whole body bound in black thread.
Tian Fu and Wu Qu. The storehouse star and the Metal general. Both are normally incredibly bright.
Wu Qu is tied up. Those threads came from the crow's feather.
The bound star groaned, a low cry edged with metal. Neo caught his breath. The same sound came from inside his body.
“...A child of Metal. Don't come. These threads eat Metal.”
I knew when I came. Do I cut them?
“Cut them, and they grow again. Uproot them. Their root is planted in the chest of the child on that judgment bench.”
With fingertip blades, Neo severed five threads. The cut ends twisted like snakes and sprang at his arm.
Neo!
Black threads climbed his wrist, past the elbow, to shoulder and neck. Ash gray spread to the ends of his silver hair.
Ghh...!
Mr. Cat, stop! The more Metal cuts, the more Obstruction moves into Metal!
Yundal extended his right hand. The hole began drawing in threads. Several vanished inside. By that same amount, cracks along the hole's rim spread toward his wrist.
Yundal, stop! Your hand is splitting!
Fine. Still only the wrist.
What's wrong with all of you?! Why do you all only say you're fine?!
Yeoni's voice struck the iron walls and rang. Hurting Officer's fire flared. And Yeoni saw Neo flinch.
...Sorry. Shouted again.
No. That didn't even tickle.
A lie. More gray had spread over Neo's neck. Instead of speaking, Yeoni clenched their fists. Nails dug into palms.
(Speak, and he hurts. Hold it in, and everyone hurts alone. What am I supposed to do?)
The door slammed behind them. Wings beat. The figure from the judgment bench had entered.
Metal walks in of its own accord. Saves me the trouble of a trial.
Judgment. This Metal is bound to Obstruction. At noon in three days, it will be erased from this sky.
By what right?! Who are you to erase someone else's name?!
A name invites ridicule. Erase it, and nobody laughs. That is mercy.
The crow raised its hammer. But its hand shook. Whenever the black feather pulsed, its shoulders flinched.
(It hurts. That feather's eating the crow, too.)
Then Moka stepped forward. The gray had left his face. Not because Yundal returned his light. Moka had shaken it off himself.
Hey.
Otter. Confiscated for the crime of rhythm.
You know that rhythm, too. The one we practiced behind the sunrise stage.
Moka's tail tapped the floor. Tap, tap, tap. A pause, then tap.
The hammer fell from the crow's hand. Its impact on the iron floor echoed for a long time.
...How do you know that rhythm?
Museong. It's you.
